blocks.text: Original document: [docs/TRACK_BUILDER_AND_ANIMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/TRACK_BUILDER_AND_ANIMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

In programmatic vector motion engines, creating complex composite UI widgets, HUD panels, and multi-part diagrammatic entities often requires coordinating multiple sub-animations (e.g., drawing borders, handwriting labels, revealing status badges, tracing sparklines, and fading in subtitles).
Prior to this architecture, orchestrating such composite entities suffered from several core pain points:

items: **Scattered Animation Logic**: Animation code lived outside the entity in procedural scripts, destroying encapsulation.
**Manual Timestamp Arithmetic**: Developers had to manually compute start delays (`delay: 450`, `delay: 1100`), making maintenance brittle whenever a duration changed.
**Squashing vs. Stretching**: Generic group animations redistributed timings via `lagRatio`, distorting fine-tuned sub-animation choreography.
**Rigid Introducers**: Calling `scene.play(new Create(myCompositeWidget))` would either naively traverse low-level geometries simultaneously or fail to animate custom components properly.

blocks.text: Retiam introduces the **Track-Based Animation Subsystem** via [`TrackBuilder`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/TrackBuilder.ts), [`TrackAnimation`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/TrackAnimation.ts), and the `Entity.createAnim()` hook. This architecture enables entities to encapsulate their own multi-stage entrance choreography while exposing an ergonomic, declarative API.

items: **Co-located Lifecycle**: Entities define their entrance animation directly within their class definition via `createAnim(t: TrackBuilder)`.
**Zero Timestamp Arithmetic**: Developers declare sequential steps, parallel clusters, and temporal pauses without manual millisecond tracking.
**Natural Duration Retention**: When played with `new Create(entity)`, the animation automatically calculates and adopts the natural timeline duration of its constituent tracks.

**Proportional Duration Scaling**: If the caller explicitly provides a custom duration (e.g. `new Create(entity, { duration: 3000, rate_func: Rate.easeInOutCubic() })`), all child durations and relative start delays scale proportionally without manual intervention.

**Universal Introducer Integration**: [`Create`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/creation/Create.ts) automatically detects the `createAnim` hook and delegates to it seamlessly, while continuing to provide standard geometry stroke tracing for basic entities.

**Polymorphic Return Support**: An entity can use `t.add(...)` and return `void` (compiled via `TrackBuilder`), or return a custom [`Animation`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/Animation.ts) instance directly.

blocks.text: [`TrackBuilder.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/TrackBuilder.ts) is a lightweight fluent utility for accumulating animations and computing relative delay offsets:

items: Tracks an internal `playhead` (in milliseconds, initialized to 0).
Appends animations to an internal array `anims: Animation[]`.
Computes `stepDuration = max(localDelay + anim.duration)` for each step.
Advances `playhead` by `stepDuration` on `.add()` and by `ms` on `.wait(ms)`.
Overrides total duration calculation:
Preserves pre-computed sub-animation delays without overwriting them through `lagRatio`.

When a caller specifies a target duration $D_{\text{target}}$ on `Create(entity, { duration: D_target })`:

items: `TrackAnimation` calculates its natural duration $D_{\text{natural}}$.
If $D_{\text{natural}} > 0$ and $D_{\text{target}} \neq D_{\text{natural}}$, a scalar ratio $S = \frac{D_{\text{target}}}{D_{\text{natural}}}$ is calculated.
